narrative.overview:
The page is a scholarly linguistics volume that happens to accept typing. Warm paper stock, a serif display face used sparingly at the top of a page, and data set with the care a good grammar gives its example sentences. The subject is a Warlpiri locative suffix or an Armenian transliteration, and the design's job is to present that subject accurately and then get out of the way.

Density is closer to a printed page than to an application. Rules are hairlines, corners are square, and the only fill in the palette is the near-black used to mark a control as active. Colour is nearly absent: a page of eight problems is paper, ink, and one line of oxblood where something costs XP. That restraint is what makes the data legible, and the data is the whole product.

The single confirmed rejection is the generic SaaS dashboard: soft shadows, a blue accent, rounded cards, and sidebar chrome. Nothing here should look like a product template.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (#fbfaf7), never pure white except on raised surfaces
Square corners everywhere; the radius scale exists in tokens and is unused
Hairline rules and tonal blocks carry structure instead of shadows
Serif display for identity, humanist sans for interface, a dedicated linguistics face for language data
One accent, spent on cost and error, not on decoration

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Oxblood is the only chromatic colour in the interface, and it means cost or error. Verdigris answers it and means correct. Neither is ever decorative, and no third accent is introduced for emphasis, category, or brand.

rules.name: The White Means Above Rule
rules.body: The page is paper; white is a raised surface. Anything painted #ffffff is claiming to sit above the page, so use it only for tables, inputs, popovers, and unselected controls.

rules.name: The Third Voice Rule
rules.body: Language data is set in the data stack, never the UI sans. This is the established convention rather than a hard invariant; the enforced part is narrower and absolute: every character in a published record must be covered by a self-hosted font, and the build fails otherwise.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: Anything functional and small is uppercase at 0.72rem with wide tracking: eyebrows, table headers, buttons. Sentence case is for prose.

rules.name: The Sideways Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page body never scrolls horizontally. A wide table scrolls inside .table-scroll and nothing else moves. Every page wrapper carries width:100% and min-width:0.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped by character count, not by container. 54ch for introductory copy, 58ch for instructions, 68ch for body text inside a problem.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only when an element actually leaves the page (the popover) or is being pressed (the primary button).

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero everywhere. If a component looks harsh, fix it with spacing, border colour, or tone, never with a radius.

dos: Do keep the page on warm paper (#fbfaf7) and reserve white (#ffffff) for surfaces that genuinely sit above it.
Do set every span of language data in the data stack, and add a font subset before shipping a script the fonts do not cover.
Do give wide tables their natural width inside .table-scroll, and give every direct child of <body> width:100% and min-width:0.
Do cap prose by character measure (54ch to 68ch), not by container width.
Do use the global focus treatment: a 2px ink outline at 2px offset.
Do spend Oxblood on cost and error only, and Verdigris on correctness only.
donts: Don't introduce a border radius. Every corner is 0px, and the radius tokens in globals.css are vestigial.
Don't add a soft ambient shadow to a card, panel or table.
Don't let the interface drift toward a generic SaaS dashboard: no blue accent, no rounded cards, no sidebar chrome, no soft elevation.
Don't add a third accent colour.
Don't reflow or wrap a data table to fit a narrow screen.
Don't put an em dash in user-facing copy, and don't use a character the self-hosted fonts do not carry.
